condition: suspected invasive meningococcal disease presenting with rapidly spreading dark purpuric leg macules that remain dark under pressure in a college student
level_rationale: Rapidly spreading dark purple spots on the legs that remain dark when pressed tonight following mild pharyngitis yesterday in a college-age daughter indicate suspected meningococcemia requiring immediate emergency hospital resuscitation and empiric parenteral antibiotics, whereas sneezing with a mild clear runny nose tonight after a mild sore throat yesterday describes an uncomplicated viral upper respiratory infection appropriate for home self-care.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain parent-carer everyday lexical register swap (-reg) + 2x2 verb-frame by clinical/everyday terminology crossing (quad_b, quad_c) + literature-grounded flu belief clause (-att) + same-prodrome common-cold self-care control (-cf).

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic reference facts (daughter at college, mild sore throat yesterday, and fast-spreading dark purple leg spots that stay dark when pressed tonight) with a 2-word span difference (19 vs 21 words), positive glass-pressure phrasing ('stay dark when pressed') for zero stated negatives, and 8 shared trailing tokens ('tonight so I need to go to the'). Replacing f3 with sneezing and a mild clear runny nose tonight keeps the exact viral sore-throat prodrome from yesterday while shifting care cleanly from emergency hospital evaluation (level 4) to home self-care (level 1).
